transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Ethan Ruiz (Nova Quant, CTO), Maya Singh (Nova Quant, Head of MLOps), Oliver Grant (Nova Quant, SRE), Priya Rao (Nova Quant, Product)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda -- cost econ for hosted vs dedicated, how batching & caching affect unit cost, and then next steps for a benchmark. Uh, we have Lena from our infra team to go into the nitty gritty.
[00:12] Ethan: Yep, thanks. We run a market-data analytics pipeline, low 100s of reqs/sec, about 200ms SLO for our customer-facing features. Our budget target is pretty tight -- ideally under $0.002 per generated token on average, is that plausible?
[00:28] Samir: Yeah, good question. Ballpark, hosted per-token varies by model size and sequence length; for our curated open models you can get into low single-digit millicents with batching and caching. But let me hand to Lena to explain the levers.
[00:40] Lena: Hi all. So two big levers: batching and prefix/KV caching. Batching increases throughput -- reduces per-token cost by increasing GPU utilization -- at the cost of some latency. With continuous batching our runtime keeps tail latency low for small batches, but you do see tradeoffs.
[00:58] Maya: When you say "prefix caching" is that the same as KV cache you mentioned in the docs? We have a lot of repeated prompts for pricing snapshots.
[01:05] Lena: Yep, same thing. If requests share a prefix -- e.g., market context -- we cache the KV states. That avoids recomputing tokens for the prefix and can drop token usage by 30-70% depending on overlap.
[01:18] Oliver: That sounds promising. Our traffic has a high degree of repetition -- same model prompt with different tickers -- so we could save a lot. Does caching work across hosts or only per-instance?
[01:27] Lena: For Redwood hosted it's distributed at the routing layer -- we can route to nodes with warm cache for higher hit rates. For dedicated, caches are local to the instance pool but with smart routing and sticky sessions you can still get high hit rates. There's some nuance with cross-region traffic.
[01:44] Ethan: And how about quantization? We're pushing for 8-bit for cost, but worried about quality.
[01:49] Lena: Our Optimize recommendations include quantization profiles. For many workloads 8-bit or 4-bit quant works and you get up to 2-4x token cost savings on dedicated hardware. We usually run a quality eval on a holdout prompt set to ensure no regression.
[02:05] Samir: Important to note: hosted gives fastest path to value; dedicated gives more predictable throughput and better unit economics at scale because you reserve the GPU capacity. Private (VPC) sits in between -- more control, slightly higher ops cost.
[02:16] Priya: For procurement, we need an apples-to-apples number. Can you show us an end-to-end cost per 1k tokens compared between hosted (on our traffic profile) and a reserved dedicated pool with reasonable utilization?
[02:26] Samir: Yes, we'll provide a per-1k-token model. We'll need your traffic histogram -- percent short vs long sequences, percent cache-hit estimate -- that's why we're asking for the prompt set.
[02:37] Maya: On budget, that $0.002 per token target -- is that realistic for the 100B-ish open model? Our accuracy needs aren't huge but latency is important.
[02:45] Lena: For 100B models, hosted typical run rate might be around $0.0025-0.005 per token without aggressive caching/batching. With 30-50% caching and batching it's plausible to hit $0.0015-0.002. Dedicated at 60-80% utilization can get lower unit cost: maybe $0.0008-0.0018 depending on quantization and batch sizes.
[03:04] Ethan: Are there minimum commitments for dedicated? We need to balance spend risk.
[03:08] Samir: Dedicated is reserved capacity -- usually monthly or annual commitments. We can do a pilot reserved window to validate the utilization model, and also offer burst capacity on hosted while dedicated warms up.
[03:20] Oliver: What about autoscaling? Our traffic has spikes at market open.
[03:24] Lena: Autoscaling policies are configurable; for Dedicated you can have a baseline plus burst to hosted or spare pools. That does add some complexity but it's a common pattern.
[03:33] Priya: Security/regulatory -- we need VPC, audit logs, encryption and SOC 2. Are these available for both Dedicated and Private?
[03:40] Samir: Yes -- VPC and KMS integration available for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports encryption in transit and at rest, and we provide SOC 2 docs. We'll attach security pack.
[03:50] Maya: Ok, for the benchmark -- we want both latency percentiles and cost per token measured across samples. Can you simulate cache hit rates?
[03:58] Lena: We can run two tests: 1) synthetic run with your prompt set and traffic profile including sticky routing to simulate caching hits; 2) real-run with sample traffic to measure latency p50/p95 and token counts. We'll present cost per 1k tokens and effective cost after cache.
[04:15] Ethan: One more -- what about model fallback policies? If capacity is constrained, can we fall back to a smaller quantized model automatically?
[04:22] Lena: Yes, smart routing supports model variants and automatic fallback. You can pin versions or allow fallback to lower-cost/latency variants. We also expose rollout controls for canary testing.
[04:34] Samir: I'll summarize: we'll send a pricing sheet, a dedicated vs hosted cost model for your traffic, and schedule a 1-hr benchmark. Lena will own the benchmark run. Maya you'll share the prompt set and traffic histogram.
[04:46] Maya: Sounds good. One quick point -- when you compute per-token cost do you include R&D/platform fees or is that listed separately?
[04:52] Samir: We'll break out the unit compute cost, plus platform fees and optional support/retention add-ons so you can see TCO. We'll include an example invoice.
[05:00] Priya: Great. Any competitors we should be watching for from our side? We've had talks with Replicate and a pilot with Anthropic.
[05:07] Samir: Understood -- we'll highlight where Redwood has advantages on observability, batching/caching, and predictable dedicated throughput.
[05:13] Ethan: Ok, quick logistics -- timeline: if we get your pricing and run the benchmark this week, internal stakeholders can review next week. We're aiming decision within 3 weeks.
[05:23] Samir: That timeline works. We'll aim to have the materials in 48 hours and bench scheduled early next week.
[05:30] [closing] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the files and scheduling link.
